texts.preamble: Anil S/O. Bandulal Pardeshi vs The State Of Maharashtra on 13 February, 2020 Author: Mangesh S. Patil Bench: Mangesh S. Patil 3.Aba.19.2020. In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad 3 Anticipatory Bail Application No.19 Of 2020 Anil s/o Bandulal Pardeshi, Age : 37 years, Occu: Driver, R/o. Holkar Nagar, Tq. Ambad, Dist. Jalna. ... Applicant Versus The State of Maharashtra, through Ambad, Police Station, Jalna. ... Respondent ... Advocate for Applicant : Mr. Uttarwar Pavan P. App for Respondent/State: G.L. Deshpande ... Coram : Mangesh S. Patil, J. Date : .13.02.2020 Per Court : The applicant is seeking bail in anticipation of his arrest in connection with Crime No.499/2019 registered with Ambad Police Station, Ambad for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 26, 26(2) (Iv), 27(2) (e) of Section 59 of the Standards Food and Safety Act, 2006. 2. It is alleged that on 29.11.2019, in the wee hours a vehicle being driven by the applicant was accosted and some prohibited articles like scented tobacco, Zafrani Zarda, Pan Masala etc., was found being transported in the vehicle.
texts.facts: The applicant is seeking bail in anticipation of his arrest in connection with Crime No.499/2019 registered with Ambad Police Station, Ambad for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 26, 26(2) (Iv), 27(2) (e) of Section 59 of the Standards Food and Safety Act, 2006. 2. It is alleged that on 29.11.2019, in the wee hours a vehicle being driven by the applicant was accosted and some prohibited articles like scented tobacco, Zafrani Zarda, Pan Masala etc., was found being transported in the vehicle. The substance was seized. The FIR was lodged 3.ABA.19.2020.odt by the Food Inspector and the crime was registered.
texts.arguments: The learned advocate for the applicant submits that accepting the allegations in the FIR, since there are no allegations about the articles having been administered to anybody, provision of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would not be applicable. The rest of the offences being bailable and the Muddemal having been already recovered. His presence behind the bar is not necessary to complete the investigation. He is ready to cooperate the investigating officer and he may be released on bail. 4. The learned A.P.P. opposes the application. She submits that the question whether Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would be applicable is a matter to be inquired into and decided by the trial court. The applicant has been found in possession of those articles. The applicant is a habitual offender. Even earlier on two occasions he has been involved in a similar kind of offence. There is every possibility of his indulging in similar crime and the application may be rejected.
